emergency procedure.body:
when the siren sounds:
1. stop what you are doing.
2. go to the nearest exit.
3. assemble at the car park.
4. wait for a head count.

the siren is tested every shift. a test is not an emergency.
emergency procedure.title: emergency procedure

history.body:
1974 site chosen on the grass plains above the river.
1979 construction begins.
1984 unit 1 reaches first power.
1986 unit 2 reaches first power.
2024 control room refitted with new displays (you are looking at them).
history.title: history

hot work permit.body:
welding and grinding need a hot work permit, a fire watch, and a cleared 10 m radius.

the extraction hood must run for the whole job. gas cylinders are chained when stored and capped when moved. you can pick the loose ones up with [f].
hot work permit.title: hot work permit

how a pressurised water reactor works.body:
1. the reactor core heats water to 325 c. it is kept at 155 bar so it never boils.

2. that hot water flows through steam generators, boiling a separate loop of water into steam.

3. the steam spins the turbine, which turns the generator.

4. the spent steam is condensed and cooled in the cooling towers. what you see rising from the towers is harmless water vapour.
how a pressurised water reactor works.title: how a pressurised water reactor works

naicol reactor in numbers.body:
two pwr units, 1100 mwe each.
six coolant loops (three per unit).
three control rod banks per unit.
four cooling tower cells in two 96 m towers.
one 400 kv switchyard with four bays, 800 mw each.
fuel: uranium dioxide, 18-month cycle.
spent fuel pool: 9 m deep, 38 c.
naicol reactor in numbers.title: naicol reactor in numbers

primary chemistry limits.body:
boron: set by reactivity, 0 to 1800 ppm
lithium: 0.7 to 3.5 ppm, tracks the boron
ph at 25 c: 6.9 to 7.4
dissolved hydrogen: 25 to 50 cc/kg
chloride and fluoride: below 0.15 ppm
oxygen: below 0.005 ppm

samples are taken from the hot leg, cooled and de-pressurised in the sample station before analysis.
primary chemistry limits.title: primary chemistry limits

primary coolant: sample results.body:
unit 1  on line
boron 620 ppm   lithium 1.71 ppm
ph 7.05   hydrogen 34.0 cc/kg
activity 1.10 mbq/g   chloride <0.05 ppm

unit 2  on line
boron 620 ppm   lithium 1.71 ppm
ph 7.15   hydrogen 36.5 cc/kg
activity 1.10 mbq/g   chloride <0.05 ppm

all values within limits.
primary coolant: sample results.title: primary coolant: sample results

radiological zones.body:
white: unrestricted
yellow: controlled, badge and dosimeter
orange: radiation area, 0.05 to 1 msv per hour
red: high radiation, entry only with a permit and a survey

the radwaste hall is a controlled area. everything leaving it is monitored at the hand + foot gate.
radiological zones.title: radiological zones

reception.body:
welcome to naicol reactor.

the station is open to guided visitors. please stay on the marked paths, do not enter the reactor containments, and keep away from the switchyard fence.

the control building is open to the public gallery only, but the operators have left the consoles unlocked for this open day. feel free to look around, and to try the controls.

air raid shelter, first aid and the cafe are to the east of the plaza.
reception.title: reception

safety rules.body:
stay on marked paths.
hard hat and dosimeter inside the fenced area.
no entry into any reactor containment.
the fuel pool is a radiation area: keep behind the rails.
in an emergency, follow the siren procedure on the red poster.
safety rules.title: safety rules

scale model.body:
1:500 model of the site.

two identical units sit side by side: each has a domed reactor containment, an auxiliary building and a turbine hall about 160 m long. the fuel handling building stands between them.

cooling water runs in a closed loop to two natural-draught towers, 96 m tall.
scale model.title: scale model

shielded transport cask.body:
a lead-lined cask for low and intermediate level waste. the drums go in from the top, the lid is bolted and the cask is monitored before it leaves the site.

the trefoil is the international sign for ionising radiation.
shielded transport cask.title: shielded transport cask

site map.body:
main gate ........ west
visitor centre ... north of the gate road
control building . behind the plaza
unit 1 ........... north of the central avenue
unit 2 ........... south of the central avenue
fuel building .... between the units
cooling towers ... east
switchyard ....... south-east corner
airfield ......... 600 m west of the gate
site map.title: site map

spent fuel pool.body:
water depth 9.0 m.
temperature 38 c.
the blue glow of the racks is cherenkov radiation: charged particles moving faster than light does in water.

the pool is cooled by its own loop and has two independent make-up water supplies.
spent fuel pool.title: spent fuel pool

training: reactor physics.body:
today: xenon after a power change.

xenon-135 builds up after a power reduction and peaks about 9 hours later. it eats neutrons, so the operators need more reactivity than they expect.

the training simulator in the old wing runs the same plant you can see out of the window.
training: reactor physics.title: training: reactor physics

waste drums.body:
every drum has a number, a content record, a dose rate on contact, and a date. evaporator concentrate is mixed with cement in the drum itself, so it cannot spill.

empty drums outside the cage are free to move, but please do not roll them down the road.
waste drums.title: waste drums

lock-out / tag-out: no tag, no touch. ever.
